## Rule

Filling Regions (NOT a perfect-25 identity/transpose — the ceiling-audit rumor is DISPROVEN).
Colors present: input {0,5}, output {0,2,5}. 10x10 active grid at canvas [0:10,0:10].
- Gray-5 markers on the TOP ROW (row 0) mark those COLUMNS.
- Gray-5 markers on the RIGHT COLUMN (col 9) mark those ROWS.
- Output = keep every input marker (5), and paint red-2 at every interior (marked row x marked
  col) intersection. Marker cells themselves stay 5.

## Algorithm sketch

```
colmask[w] = input[0,w] == 5      # top-row markers -> marked columns
rowmask[r] = input[r,9] == 5      # right-col markers -> marked rows
out[r,w] = 5 if input[r,w]==5 else (2 if rowmask[r] and colmask[w] else 0)
```
LIVE realizes this as ONE free-output Einsum (memory=0): a rank-2 bilinear
rowdet(k,r)=C[k,color(r,9)], coldet(k,w)=C[k,color(0,w)], combined via M and output-mapped by
C, gated by cur(r,w)=sum_l C[l,color(r,w)] whose sign preserves markers. Decode is STRICT
one-hot: harness assigns color c iff exactly one channel > 0 (NOT argmax).

## Cost analysis

score_v2(live) = (macs 0, memory 0, cost 84). Cost counts initializer ELEMENTS (not bytes):
C[2,10]=20 + M[2,2]=4 + right_col[30]=30 + top_row[30]=30 = 84. memory=0 because the single
Einsum writes the one-hot output directly (free output) — no materialized intermediate.

Floor proof (84 is the floor for this einsum family):
- **Selectors 60 forced-or-53-via-share.** Each selector contracts input's length-30 spatial
  axis, so each is a length-30 dense initializer. Shortening (crop) is scorer-invalid; sparse
  inits are rank-rejected (both dead, see hard_records). The ONLY sub-84 lever is sharing the two
  selectors into one -> 54. That route is strict-decode-INFEASIBLE (below).
- **C=20 forced (rank-2).** The AND-intersection (red only when row AND col marked) is a rank-2
  bilinear: a rank-1 read C[1,10] gives rowdet,coldet in {C[0],C[5]} whose products for MM and UU
  are both squares (C[5]^2, C[0]^2) -> same sign -> cannot separate red from background. Two
  layers (C[2,10]) are required.
- **M=4 forced.** Deleting M (absorb into C) makes the classifier leak wrong channels -> visible
  0/266 (hard_records/absorbed_m_liveC.md).
- **Shared-selector 54 is strict-infeasible.** Interior/generic cells ARE strictly feasible with a
  shared S, but on the marker lines (row 0, col 9) rowdet(0)/coldet(9) become data-dependent
  weighted sums over the marker pattern (Sum_x S[x]*read) instead of an isolated one-hot cell;
  no (C,M,S) satisfies the strict one-hot decode there. Verified across 4 independent solver
  formulations (2026-07-07) — all pin ~1200 failures each to row0 and col9, interior 0.

Verdict: **WALL at 84** for the free-output bilinear einsum family. A sub-84 win needs a
genuinely new contraction structure that re-prices the two marker-line reads without a second
length-30 selector — none found.

## Don't-do log

- Do NOT chase a cost-1 / perfect-25 identity/transpose/flip/rotate. AIRTIGHT DISPROOF (no gate
  needed): every input uses colors {0,5}; every output introduces color 2 (red). A zero-param
  direct-output op (Identity / any Transpose perm / flip / rotate / Slice / Gather of input cells)
  only PERMUTES existing cell values and can never introduce a new color absent from the input.
  Therefore the whole legal zero-param family is impossible by construction. It is a rank-2
  Filling Regions task; the forced floor for this task is the free-output bilinear einsum, not 1.
- Do NOT optimize the shared selector for ARGMAX correctness — the harness decodes STRICT
  one-hot (exactly one channel > 0), so argmax-feasible solutions (e.g. the cost-54 proto) fail
  visible 0/266 with npos==2. Any shared-selector solve MUST target the strict one-vs-rest decode.
- Do NOT re-run: absorb-M, output-crop, sparse-selectors, live-coeff shared selector (all dead —
  see hard_records/).
- Do NOT materialize a Slice/row0/col9 read to drop the selectors: it creates a charged
  intermediate (memory) far above the 60 selector elements; the free-output einsum (memory 0) is
  why 84 is cheap.
